claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented. claimDescriptions.plainDescription: For one caller-supplied RatifyEnv, EnactState and GovActionState, acceptedBy for a single role is evaluated exactly as in the formal Conway specification. CC counts one unit per active member (term not passed, i.e. currentEpoch ≤ term, and a registered hot credential), an active non-voting member counts as no, and when a CC threshold exists the active size must also satisfy sizeActiveCC ≥ ccMinSize. DRep counts cast votes first, then no for every other active DRep, then the predetermined votes: abstain-vdeleg always abstains and noConfidence-vdeleg votes yes only on a NoConfidence action. SPO counts cast votes first, otherwise defaults by the pool reward account's vote delegation: abstain-vdeleg abstains, noConfidence-vdeleg votes yes only on NoConfidence, a TriggerHardFork default is always no, and every other default is no, including an unregistered pool. Acceptance is yesStake ⁄₀ (yesStake+noStake) ≥ t, where ⁄₀ returns 0 on a zero denominator, t defaults to 0 when the role does not vote, and equality passes.

claimDescriptions.plainDescription: For one PParamsUpdate u against one pinned PParams pp and a Maybe ccThreshold, the thresholds are: DRep = maximum of P5a, P5b, P5c, P5d over the groups that u actually modifies (Network, Economic, Technical, Governance respectively); SPO = Q5 if and only if u modifies the SecurityGroup, otherwise SPO does not vote; CC = ccThreshold when present, or the constant 2 (which can never pass) under no-confidence. Group membership is computed field-by-field: a group is modified iff at least one of its Maybe fields is Just. In particular govActionDeposit is in both the GovernanceGroup list and the SecurityGroup list, so an update touching only govActionDeposit requires P5d for DReps and Q5 for SPOs. An update modifying no group is ill-formed (ppdWellFormed requires updateGroups ≠ ∅).

claimDescriptions.plainDescription: Over one supplied EnactState and one supplied complete ordered GovState, three separate local facts are stated and must not be conflated. (1) Enactability/connectivity: for a hash-protected action type (NoConfidence and UpdateCommittee share the cc purpose; NewConstitution; TriggerHardFork; ChangePParams), a candidate is connectable iff there exists a duplicate-free list of actions drawn from the supplied state whose prevAction links form a chain from the candidate back to the currently enacted ID for that purpose, getHashES(es, type); TreasuryWithdrawal and Info have no prevAction and are always connectable. Existence of such a witness is claimed, not uniqueness of the connecting path. (2) RATIFY-time prev check: verifyPrev holds iff the candidate's prevAction equals the current enacted ID for its type at the moment RATIFY checks it, and an action is delayed if verifyPrev fails or a prior delaying action (NoConfidence, UpdateCommittee, NewConstitution, TriggerHardFork) was accepted earlier in the same pass. (3) Orphan removal: at an epoch boundary, actions whose parent is neither enacted nor still pending are iteratively removed (getOrphans) and their deposits are refunded through the boundary refund path.

claimDescriptions.plainDescription: This row is split into two explicitly tagged profiles that share one ID lineage and must not be merged. Formal-spec profile: over a supplied, claimed-complete ordered event list for one DRep credential c, expiry(c) is set to e + drepActivity at registration or re-registration and refreshed at every transaction in epoch e carrying a vote by c; at every epoch boundary whose post-removal governance state (govSt') is empty, the expiry of every DRep is incremented by 1 (the EPOCH Pre-POOLREAPUpdate applies mapValues sucᵉ to the whole DReps map in that case); the entry is deleted at deregdrep; c is active at epoch E iff E ≤ expiry(c). Implementation-adapter profile (unresolved): prior reviewers report that the Haskell implementation instead bumps every DRep by numDormantEpochs when a transaction carries proposals and computes voter expiry with that dormant count; whether and how that mechanism is equivalent to the formal fold is not established by any body in this bundle.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Epoch arithmetic over range-bounded naturals: expiresIn = s + L; voting-window constraint ¬(expiresIn < e) for each vote epoch e; ratification-boundary constraint R ≥ s+1 with acceptance checked before expiry so R ≤ s+L+1 on the accept branch; delay-branch constraint that once a delaying action is accepted in a pass, no later candidate in that pass is accepted; effect-epoch constraints effect = R+1 on the accept branch and refund-effect = s+L+2 on the never-accepted-and-never-orphaned branch; orphan branch requires a prior orphan-removal witness (CAP-C-004 lineage) and forbids the s+L+2 expiry schedule. All branches are mutually exclusive tags; no branch may be inferred from arithmetic alone without its branch witness.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Branch witnesses: for acceptance, the RATIFIES accept trace at R; for expiry, the reject trace at s+L+1; for orphan removal, the getOrphans trace; for delay, the earlier accepted delaying action in the same pass.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; proposal epoch s; govActionLifetime L at s; expiresIn = s+L; optional ratification boundary R; branch tag ∈ {accepted, expired, orphan-removed, delayed-then-accepted, pending}; derived public epochs for enactment effect and deposit-pot exit; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: None for the spec schedule. Any statement about a real action's epochs requires authenticated observation of the proposing slot, the boundary transitions and the refund through replay (CAP-C-016 lineage), plus the premise that the chain actually progresses to those boundaries; the schedule proves no liveness.
claimDescriptions.limitations: This is a derivation from the formal specification only; no node conformance is observed in this bundle, and no Agda was typechecked or executed here. The schedule assumes the action record's expiresIn is set from govActionLifetime at the proposing epoch, as in the assigned row's GOV-Propose reference; Gov.lagda.md itself is not in this bundle.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented, and a Groth16 proof is unnecessary for this arithmetic; a host checker is the proportionate tool. If encoded anyway, the UInt128/R1CS slice would still need the branch witnesses above, which it does not provide. First blocker: a complete branch/domain specification including prior orphan removal and progression of the chain; for a real action, authenticated transition evidence.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: For one governance action proposed in epoch s with govActionLifetime L at s, the formal-spec schedule is conditional on the action surviving as pending and on the chain progressing. expiresIn = s + L. Votes are accepted in transactions of epochs s through s+L, because the vote premise fails exactly when expiresIn < e. RATIFIES at the boundary into epoch R (with s+1 ≤ R) uses the votes and state after the previous boundary's removals, and because RATIFY-Accept is checked before expiry, acceptance at R = s+L+1 is still possible. If accepted at R, the new EnactState, treasury-withdrawal payout and deposit refund take effect through the next boundary, into R+1. If the action is never accepted and is not removed earlier as an orphan, RATIFY-Reject fires at the boundary into s+L+1 and the deposit leaves the pot through the boundary into s+L+2. Accepting a delaying action (NoConfidence, UpdateCommittee, NewConstitution, TriggerHardFork) blocks every later candidate in the same RATIFIES pass. An action removed as an orphan at an earlier boundary follows the orphan path instead and does not wait until s+L+2.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: This is not one relation. Each sub-claim needs its own relation over authenticated input and output boundary states: the RATIFIES trace relation must check every action in the ordered pass in order (including delay flags and ENACT premises) to establish an accept/reject event for g or the absence of both; the enacted-field relation must open the EnactState current in epoch E+1 and compare the relevant purpose field (or, for TreasuryWithdrawal, the accumulated withdrawals and their payout); the orphan relation must run the full getOrphans fixed point; the pending relation must prove membership of g in the post-boundary GovState together with completeness of that state. Bounded list lengths and per-transition step bounds must be public.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Either a complete replay trace from an authenticated starting state to the two boundary states, or authenticated state openings (inclusion and, where needed, non-membership/completeness proofs) for RatifyState, EnactState and GovState at the named cutpoints.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier (named finality rule, fork, epoch and boundary cutpoint); GovActionID g; boundary epoch E; sub-claim tag ∈ {ratified@E, enacted-field@E+1, rejected-expired@E, orphan-removed@E, pending@E}; the resulting status payload for that sub-claim only; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: A certified governance/epoch state or replay from genesis with a pinned node and a named finality rule; provider API responses are labelled premises only. Negative and pending conclusions require completeness of the RatifyState/GovState at the cutpoint. A SNARK may compress a verified replay but cannot authenticate a prover-chosen root, snapshot or epoch state.
claimDescriptions.limitations: Within the formal model the two-stage pipeline is exact: EPOCH first processes the previous boundary's removed set and orphans, then runs RATIFIES on the surviving state. Any single-epoch status language that collapses these stages is unsound. No anchor exists in this bundle; every sub-claim is therefore currently unprovable for Preprod, and this row proposes structure only.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; the UInt128/R1CS slice provides no replay, state-commitment, Mithril-verifier, or governance transition circuits, and existing genuine current-Rust invoice/VK artefacts (per task premise) do not establish any of these predicates. Needed: an authenticated-state or replay-compression specification with explicit transition-step bounds; indexed historical authentication cost is unknown. First blocker: no certified governance state on Preprod and no defined certified governance root; replay is the only currently describable path.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: The single status enum in the original row is split, under this same ID, into four separately timed queries about one GovActionID g at one boundary on one fork. (a) Ratified-at-E: RATIFY-Accept fired for g during the RATIFIES pass of the EPOCH transition into E. (b) Enacted-field-at-E+1: the EnactState produced by that pass is the one current in epoch E+1, and for hash-protected purposes its purpose ID equals g; for TreasuryWithdrawal the effect is the accumulated payout at E+1, and for Info this never occurs. (c) Removed-at-E, with two distinct causes that must be distinguished: RATIFY-Reject fired for g in the pass into E (expired), or g was removed by getOrphans during GovernanceUpdate at E. (d) Pending-at-E: g is a member of the complete post-boundary GovState at E. These are not mutually exclusive across different boundaries, and a final purpose ID alone can hide an intermediate accepted update in the same pass, so each sub-claim is stated and proved separately.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Complete-map openings (sorted exhaustive scans) for members and ccHotKeys; per-member active predicate (E ≤ term) ∧ (hot lookup = Just h); cardinality computed over the complete active set with bounded size; quorum comparison reuses the CAP-C-001 CC constraints; the no-confidence case is an explicit None tag on the public side, and any threshold-2 encoding must be derived from that tag, never from an arbitrary map.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Complete members and ccHotKeys maps with exhaustive openings; ccMinSize from the authenticated parameter set at the same cutpoint.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier with epoch E and the exact boundary/block cutpoint at which hot keys are read; public option: None (no-confidence) or Some (commitment to the complete members map, rational threshold q as reduced num/den); commitment to the complete ccHotKeys map at the same cutpoint; active-set commitment and its cardinality; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016. The active set and its cardinality are completeness statements: isolated membership proofs for individual members cannot establish them. Hot keys can change mid-epoch, so the authentication must be at the same cutpoint at which RATIFY would read them (the RatifyEnv ccHotKeys supplied by EPOCH).
claimDescriptions.limitations: EPOCH prunes ccHotKeys to current committee members (ccCreds) when producing gState', while the RATIFY environment at a boundary is built from the pre-existing LState; a claim must state which of these states its hot-key map comes from. Real-world identity or conduct of members is outside the claim.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; no complete-map, cardinality, or rational-quorum governance circuit exists in the UInt128/R1CS slice. Needed: a complete-map opening specification with cardinality and the CAP-C-001 CC tally as a shared primitive. First blocker: authenticated state at a named boundary cutpoint.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: At a named epoch E and a named boundary cutpoint, the EnactState cc field is either nothing (no-confidence) or just (members, q), where members maps cold credentials to term epochs and q is the rational committee threshold. The active set at that cutpoint is {c ∈ members | E ≤ term(c) and ccHotKeys[c] = just h} — a member whose term has passed, whose hot key is unregistered, or who has resigned is inactive. Acceptance by the committee additionally requires the size of that complete active set to be at least ccMinSize. Under no-confidence, actions that would need committee approval instead carry threshold 2 and cannot pass. Whether the hot-key map is the one in the RatifyEnv at the boundary or the post-pruning map must be stated as part of the claim instance.

claimDescriptions.plainDescription: At a named epoch-boundary cutpoint, for one DRep credential c: the dreps map contains c ↦ x (expiry epoch), the recorded DRep deposit for c is dep lovelace, and c counts as active for ratification iff E ≤ x. The cutpoint must be named exactly, because the boundary itself can change the value: the EPOCH rule builds its RatifyEnv from the pre-transition DReps of the ledger state, while the post-EPOCH GState may already have had every expiry incremented by 1 when the post-removal governance state is empty; a post-EPOCH expiry must not be silently presented as the expiry used by that same boundary's ratification. Stake delegated to an inactive c is outside the active vote-delegatee set and absent from DRep voting totals.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Exact variant: complete keyed enumeration of the UTxO set, voteDelegs, stakeDelegs, rewards, deposits and mark snapshot at the cutpoint; per-credential stake = UTxO coin for outputs whose stake credential is c, plus c's governance-action deposit stake, plus rewards[c]; aggregation by vote-delegatee over activeVDelegs only, and by pool over the mark snapshot plus governance deposits restricted to registered pools; all sums over bounded lovelace with limb range checks and no wrap; distinct-key constraints throughout. Lower-bound variant: only distinct authenticated summands under the same root and delegation state, with an explicit ≥ constraint; it must never be presented as exact or as an upper bound.

claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier with boundary epoch E and cutpoint; variant tag ∈ {exact, lower-bound}; the queried VDeleg or pool KeyHash; the resulting amount in lovelace (exact) or the proven lower bound; maximum state-size and lovelace bit-length bounds; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016, with completeness over every summand for the exact variant. A Mithril stake-distribution artefact covers pool stake for block production and is the wrong object for DRep voting stake; offering it as DRep stake is refused at the anchor stage. Delegators' endorsement of their delegatee's votes is not established by stake totals.
claimDescriptions.limitations: The governance-deposit contribution to pool voting stake is a deliberate deviation from the original CIP-1694 intent, recorded as an erratum in the source itself; the code is followed and the erratum preserved. Spec/node conformance of the live-UTxO choice is unobserved in this bundle.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; the UInt128/R1CS slice has no complete-state enumeration, snapshot, or aggregation circuits for governance maps. Needed: a complete-state aggregation specification (exact) and a distinct-membership lower-bound primitive sharing one authenticated root. First blocker: no certified complete state or cutpoint codec; Mithril artefacts do not fill this gap.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: This row is split into an exact variant and a lower-bound variant under one ID. Exact: at boundary E, stakeDistrVDeleg(vd) is the sum, over every credential c whose vote delegation is vd, of the coin in UTxO outputs carrying stake credential c in the post-removal UTxO state at the boundary, plus the governance-action deposits whose return address has stake credential c, plus rewards[c] — computed from the live UTxO at the boundary, not from a snapshot, and only for active vote delegatees (active DReps plus the always-abstain and always-no-confidence delegatees). stakeDistrPools(kh) is the stake delegated to kh in the new mark snapshot plus governance-action deposits of credentials stake-delegated to kh, restricted to registered pools. Lower-bound: a named delegatee or pool has at least X lovelace, proved from distinct authenticated holdings only.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Exact variant: opening of the complete GovActionState votes record for g at the named phase, or authenticated equality of its commitment with the public V digest; absence variant: authenticated non-membership of x in the relevant voter map together with a proof that g itself is in the GovState domain at that phase (so 'no vote' is not confused with 'no such action'); any derivation from transaction history must include the last-write-wins overwrite order and the rmOrphanDRepVotes filtering step as explicit transition constraints over the bounded intervening trace.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Authenticated GovState opening at the named phase, or a complete replay segment including every vote transaction and certificate transition affecting g up to that phase.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier; GovActionID g; boundary epoch E; phase tag (pre/post certificate filtering, pre/post boundary); variant tag ∈ {exact-map, voter-absent}; either the digest of V = (gvCC, gvDRep, gvSPO) or the pair (x, absent); claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016. Transaction inclusion of a vote shows only that it was cast at some point; it cannot establish the recorded map at a boundary after overwrites and deregistration filtering. Non-membership is impossible without a completeness-capable authenticated state.
claimDescriptions.limitations: Gov.lagda.md (addVote, GOV-Vote/GOV-Propose) and Gov/Properties/LastVoteApplied.lagda.md are not in this bundle; last-write-wins and the vote-application property rest on the assigned row and prior comments, while the deregistration filter actually applied by LEDGER is verified directly here. Defaults for non-voters are computed in CAP-C-001 and are not part of this claim; recorded votes alone do not prove ratification. Author packet flagged Gov/Actions/Certs/ProtocolVersion/LastVoteApplied unread; fresh Muse source audit 20261016 read them in full and found definitional grounding only, no new theorem, no ledger authentication.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; no GovState commitment, non-membership, or replay-compression circuit exists in the UInt128/R1CS slice. Needed: a committed exact vote-map opening with a sound non-membership structure, or bounded replay compression. First blocker: no authenticated state with completeness/non-membership on Preprod.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: At a named boundary epoch E and a named state phase, the recorded votes on one governance action g are exactly V = (gvCC, gvDRep, gvSPO); in the absence variant, a named voter x has no recorded vote on g, which requires first establishing that g itself is present in the governance state at that phase. 'Recorded' means the state after last-write-wins across all transactions up to that phase and after removal of votes by DReps who are no longer registered (rmOrphanDRepVotes filters gvDRep by the current registered-DRep domain each time LEDGER processes a transaction). A single included vote transaction proves casting, not the recorded state.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Authenticated removal record (returnAddr, GovActionDeposit g, D) at the processing boundary; contribution constraint crediting exactly D (the recorded deposit, never a current parameter value) into the aggregated payout map; destination branch: if stake(returnAddr) is a member of the rewards domain at that cutpoint, D contributes to that credential's refund entry, otherwise D contributes to unclaimed and hence to the treasury; aggregation constraints must keep this contribution distinct inside the summed reward credit (a later balance delta alone cannot identify it).
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Replay segment or authenticated openings covering the removal set, the deposit entry, and the rewards-domain membership/non-membership at the processing cutpoint.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier; GovActionID g; recorded deposit D in lovelace; return address r; cause tag ∈ {ratified, rejected-expired, orphaned}; processing boundary epoch; destination tag ∈ {reward-account, treasury-unclaimed}; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016. The treasury branch requires authoritative non-registration at the processing cutpoint — absence from a provider response is not non-membership. Treasury totals themselves belong to a different domain and are not claimed here.
claimDescriptions.limitations: Because refunds are aggregated with treasury-withdrawal payouts into one reward credit per credential, the observable ledger effect is a contribution to an aggregate, and the claim is stated at that granularity. The conditional eventual-refunded theorem (CAP-C-026) proves deposit-pot absence under its premises; it does not prove this destination routing and must not be cited for it.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; no boundary-trace, deposit, or rewards-domain non-membership circuit exists in the UInt128/R1CS slice. Needed: an authenticated boundary-transition specification with a sound non-membership representation for the rewards domain. First blocker: no authenticated boundary trace/state on Preprod.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: For one governance action g with recorded deposit D and return address r, the destination of the refund is determined at the boundary where GovernanceUpdate processes g's removal: the boundary after ratification or rejection (the removed set produced by one boundary's RATIFIES is consumed by the next boundary's GovernanceUpdate), or the same boundary for an orphan. At that point, if the stake credential of r is registered in the rewards domain, D is credited as a contribution to that credential's aggregated reward credit; otherwise D is counted as unclaimed and added to the treasury. The amount is always the recorded deposit D, not the govActionDeposit parameter current at refund time.
claimDescriptions.reviewCommentDisposition: opus-1 retain (historical, replay) adopted. gpt-1 revise adopted: the delayed ratified/rejected path and the immediate orphan path are kept distinct, the 'n/a' completeness note is replaced by an authoritative non-registration requirement, and the aggregated-contribution granularity is made explicit. gemini-1 insufficient_evidence revised: Epoch.lagda.md is present and read, so the routing and both timings are verified here; the anchor ground is retained.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: The complete ordered RATIFIES pass must be constrained (or replayed) so the cumulative withdrawal accumulator is exact: each Enact-Wdrl step requires the sum of the previously accumulated withdrawals union the new W to be ≤ the treasury given to RATIFY; bounded lovelace sums with no wrap; ratification of g itself requires the CC and DRep-P6 threshold constraints of CAP-C-001/CAP-C-002 lineage with SPO absent; payout constraints at R+1 aggregate W with governance-action returns per reward address, then split by registered/unregistered stake credential exactly as in CAP-C-022; failure of sufficiency yields RATIFY-Continue only while the action is unexpired.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: Replay segment or authenticated openings covering the full ordered pass at R (all withdrawals accumulated before and including g), the treasury value, and the rewards domain at R+1.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; Conway era tag; authenticated anchor identifier; GovActionID g; commitment to the complete withdrawal map W; ratification boundary R; per-target public outcomes at R+1 (credited amount or unclaimed); treasury commitment at R; claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016. A single target's membership proof, or inclusion of the proposal transaction, cannot establish enactment, cumulative sufficiency, or the later aggregated credit. Recipients' real-world entitlement is not established.
claimDescriptions.limitations: The payout is an aggregated reward-account credit applied through the following boundary's Post-POOLREAPUpdate (payout = governance returns ∪⁺ enacted withdrawals), not a direct payment transaction to recipients; claims must be stated at that granularity and epoch. Treasury balance arithmetic itself belongs to a different domain and is only used here as the sufficiency premise.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; no ordered-pass, treasury, or payout-aggregation circuit exists in the UInt128/R1CS slice. Needed: a complete ordered RATIFIES/ENACT transition specification with bounded accumulation. First blocker: no authenticated treasury/governance/account state and trace on Preprod; additionally, a real Preprod withdrawal requires committee and DRep votes the operator does not control.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: For one TreasuryWithdrawal action g with withdrawal map W at ratification boundary R: ratification requires committee approval and the DRep P6 threshold (SPOs do not vote), and enactment additionally requires that the sum of all withdrawals accumulated earlier in the same ordered RATIFIES pass, together with W, is at most the treasury supplied to RATIFY. If the treasury is insufficient, the action is not rejected for that reason: it stays pending (RATIFY-Continue) and is retried at later boundaries until it expires. When it is enacted at R, then through the boundary into R+1 each target whose stake credential is registered is credited its amount in its aggregated reward account; amounts for unregistered targets are not paid out and return to the treasury as unclaimed.
claimDescriptions.reviewCommentDisposition: opus-1 retain (historical, replay) adopted. gpt-1 revise adopted: cumulative sufficiency over the whole ordered pass replaces the per-target 'n/a' completeness note, registration is evaluated at payout, and the aggregated reward-credit granularity is explicit. gemini-1 insufficient_evidence revised: Enact, Ratify and Epoch bodies are present and read here; the anchor ground is retained.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Historical part: authenticated opening of the EnactState pv field at E and equality with (v, gHF). Local proposal part: pvCanFollow constraints over major/minor successors and the pending-predecessor branch — these cannot be finalised from this bundle because the ProtocolVersion body is not in it, and are therefore stated as an unresolved sub-relation, not encoded. Every public statement must carry the era tag, and a bootstrap-profile tag (per ConwayBootstrap.md) distinct from the protocol version; no constraint may equate protocol version with a node software version.

claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: Pinned VK identifier; era tag fixed to Conway for every instance of this claim; authenticated anchor identifier with epoch E; protocol version v as (major, minor); the enacting action ID gHF (bound publicly, since the statement asserts the pair); claim-policy identifier.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: As CAP-C-016. A provider-reported protocol version, an address network tag, or a script-context field cannot select a trusted chain, era, or node build. Era, bootstrap profile, and node implementation identity are three distinct facts and must be authenticated separately if claimed.
claimDescriptions.limitations: Gov.lagda.md (validHFAction) and the ProtocolVersion specification are not in this bundle, so the successor relation is not verified here and the original row's blocker is retained in that narrowed form. The bootstrap documents describe proposal/vote restrictions and initial-ID handling; they do not map bootstrap phases to protocol versions, and no such mapping is asserted. Author packet flagged Gov/Actions/Certs/ProtocolVersion/LastVoteApplied unread; fresh Muse source audit 20261016 read them in full and found definitional grounding only, no new theorem, no ledger authentication.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none implemented; no EnactState opening, era dispatch, or version-successor circuit exists in the UInt128/R1CS slice, and Dijkstra-era support must not be inferred from a Conway encoding. Needed: an authenticated epoch/era evidence specification plus the ProtocolVersion successor relation from a primary body not in this bundle. First blocker: no authenticated target-epoch/era/bootstrap evidence and no implementation correspondence.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: At a named epoch E, the EnactState pv field equals (v, gHF): a protocol version v = (major, minor) and the GovActionID that enacted it, set exactly by the Enact-HF rule when a TriggerHardFork action is enacted. Separately, as a local proposal-side fact, a TriggerHardFork proposal is acceptable only under validHFAction (its version must be able to follow the enacted version, or a pending prior hard-fork action), and the SPO default vote on a hard fork is always no regardless of reward-account delegation. Every instance of any claim in this domain must pin the era whose rules it uses; this row covers Conway rules only, and neither the protocol version nor this claim identifies which node software implements v or whether a bootstrap phase has ended.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Not applicable as a Groth16 relation. A universal certificate would have to verify a checked derivation of the exact conditional theorem, binding every premise including RTC-All (InvariantAt gaid gaSt) evidence and the abstract TxId-freshness assumption to a named formal profile; a finite encoded relation over chosen states cannot discharge a universal premise about all reachable states, and hashing the theorem statement or a predicate name proves nothing.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: None. For a future checked certificate: the full premise evidence, including a derivation of InvariantAt from the CHAIN rule, which does not currently exist.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: None proposed. If a checked certificate is ever produced, its public descriptor must name the theorem (GADepositsEventuallyRefunded), the module, the pinned formal-specification commit, and enumerate every premise as part of the statement — never as hidden assumptions.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: None, and none can be substituted: this is a statement inside the formal specification model. It asserts nothing about the deployed Preprod node, and an empirical observation of one refund is a companion observation, not this theorem.
claimDescriptions.limitations: The proof term is short precisely because the dynamics are assumed: RTC-All-last extracts the invariant at the final state and the rest is epoch comparison. 'Advancing beyond the deadline' is itself a premise (the CHAINS trace and its final epoch are given), so the theorem provides no liveness guarantee that any real chain will progress. Deposit-pot absence is also weaker than CAP-C-022's destination claim.
claimDescriptions.moriartyMappingAndFirstBlocker: Current Moriarty mapping: none, and none should be built for this row; the UInt128/R1CS slice is irrelevant to a universal Agda statement, and an existing local VK/invoice proof artefact establishes nothing here. First blocker: derivation of InvariantAt from actual reachable CHAIN transitions (upstream future work), and separately the fact that no Agda typechecking was performed in this review, so even the conditional proof term is source-read, not checked.
claimDescriptions.plainDescription: Strictly conditional formal-specification theorem, retained only in that form: if govDepsMatch holds at a chain state cs, if (gaid, gaSt) is in the governance state of cs, if LastEpoch(cs) ≤ expiresIn(gaSt), if a CHAINS trace extends cs to cs′, if the per-state invariant InvariantAt gaid gaSt (deposit already absent, or LastEpoch ≤ expiresIn+1) holds at every state along that trace, and if expiresIn+2 ≤ LastEpoch(cs′), then the GovActionDeposit for gaid is not in the deposit domain of cs′. The InvariantAt premise is not proved in the source: its derivation from the CHAIN rule is explicitly future work and needs an abstract TxId-freshness assumption, because a GovActionID embeds a transaction ID whose non-reuse the specification does not enforce syntactically. The conclusion is absence from the deposit pot, not receipt by any particular account, and not an unconditional refund guarantee.

claimDescriptions.groth16Constraints: Not applicable for the universal claim, and no finite substitute may be presented as one: a Groth16 relation could at most check a bounded selected trace (each selected EnactState change coincides with an epoch-crossing block), which is a different, weaker claim that would need its own ID lineage and must not reuse this row's statement. Groth16 cannot make a type declaration into an inhabited theorem.
claimDescriptions.groth16PrivateWitness: None exists. A future proof would be an Agda derivation over TICK/NEWEPOCH/CHAIN for all admitted transitions of the pinned era.
claimDescriptions.groth16PublicInputs: None proposed. Any future empirical companion must publish its bounded block range, anchor, and fork as a finite observation, explicitly not a certificate.
claimDescriptions.ledgerAuthenticationPremises: None available and none sufficient: even a fully authenticated replay of a finite range is supporting data about that range only, under a named fork and finality rule, and says nothing about Dijkstra-era chains.
claimDescriptions.limitations: The module defines the desired statement as a Type whose value is the epoch equality; there is no proof term to inspect, typecheck, or encode. Adjacent proved properties in properties.yaml (for example the govDepsMatch invariants) do not inhabit this statement and must not be cited as if they did.

claimDescriptions.plainDescription: Stated-only research obligation, refused as a claim: in the formal Conway model, if a block b takes a chain state cs to cs′ under CHAIN and the EnactState changes, then the epoch of b's slot is the successor of the last epoch of cs. At the pinned source this exists only as a definition returning a Type (the desired equality), with the proof marked 'coming soon'; there is no inhabitant, so nothing may cite it as proved, rely on it for other claims, or apply it to another era.
